title: Common maximal speed: two body types recorded by one medium

key_results.statement: All replacements leaving $C$ unchanged: $t'^A_{hh}=t^A_{hh}+\alpha^A_h$, $K'^A_h=K^A_h+Z-\alpha^A_h\mathbb 1_c$, $t'^B_{kk}=t^B_{kk}+\alpha^B_k$, $K'^B_k=K^B_k-Z-\alpha^B_k\mathbb 1_c$, with real $\alpha^A_h$, $\alpha^B_k$ and self-adjoint $Z$ arbitrary.

Under (8.1): $\bar x_a\mapsto\bar x_a+z$, $\bar x_b\mapsto\bar x_b-z$ with $z=(Z-\langle Z\rangle)\chi\in\mathcal N$, while $v_a$, $v_b$, $v^A_{\max}$, $v^B_{\max}$ are unchanged; under $\chi\mapsto e^{i\theta}\chi$: $\bar x_a,\bar x_b,v_a,v_b$ are multiplied by $e^{i\theta}$ and $v^A_{\max}$, $v^B_{\max}$ are unchanged.

Well defined: $\lVert v_a\rVert$, $\lVert v_b\rVert$, $g(v_a,v_b)$, $\lVert v_a-v_b\rVert$, $v^A_{\max}$, $v^B_{\max}$ and $v^A_{\max}/v^B_{\max}$ (if $v^B_{\max}>0$); not well defined: $\bar x_a-\bar x_b$, neither the vector nor its norm.
Exactly, $\lVert v_a(\lambda)\rVert\le\sum_{h,h'}a^A_{hh'}q_hq_{h'}\le v^A_{\max}$ for every product start and every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, in the presence of body $b$; likewise for $b$.

$a^A_{hh'}=\lvert t^A_{hh'}\rvert\,\lVert(K^A_h-K^A_{h'}-\langle K^A_h-K^A_{h'}\rangle)\chi\rVert$, so $v^A_{\max}$ depends only on the off-diagonal $t^A$, the differences of the $K^A_h$ and $\chi$, not on $C_B$, $K^B_k$ or $\vartheta$.

$v^T_{\max}=2\eta_Td_1^T\cos\frac{\pi}{L_T+1}\to2\eta_Td_1^T$ for $L_T\to\infty$: $2t_T\sigma_{X_T}$ for a chain type and $\tau_T\kappa_T\sigma_{X_T}$ for a Model D type, independent of $m_T$, $N_T$, $\lambda_{0T}$.

Exactly, $v^A_{\max}=v^B_{\max}$ iff $t_A\sigma_{X_A}=t_B\sigma_{X_B}$ for chain types, and iff $\tau_A\kappa_A\sigma_{X_A}=\tau_B\kappa_B\sigma_{X_B}$ for Model D types (chains on $\mathbb Z$, or finite chains of equal length).
Laws 1-5 and A1-A9 do not imply $v^A_{\max}=v^B_{\max}$: admissible chain descriptions realize every ratio $v^A_{\max}/v^B_{\max}=t_A\sigma_{X_A}/(t_B\sigma_{X_B})\in(0,\infty)$.

For two chains or two Model D types with the same number $L\ge2$ of positions, a correspondence of all points exists iff $\ell_B=\pm\ell_A$, which implies $d_1^A=d_1^B$; then $v^A_{\max}=v^B_{\max}$ iff $\eta_A=\eta_B$, that is $t_A=t_B$ for chains and $\tau_A=\tau_B$ for Model D.

In the weak-record regime $\lvert\Psi(\lambda)\rangle=e^{-iC_A\lambda}\lvert\phi\rangle\otimes e^{-iC_B\lambda}\lvert\vartheta\rangle\otimes\lvert\chi\rangle+O(\kappa_A)+O(\kappa_B)$, so the view of each body is that of its own body contract alone and the one-body results of 05 and 06 apply to each body.

For equal drift speeds $\nu=\lVert\bar v_a\rVert=\lVert\bar v_b\rVert$: $R_A-R_B=\frac{\nu^2}{2}\bigl[(v^A_{\max})^{-2}-(v^B_{\max})^{-2}\bigr]+O(p_{0A}^4)+O(p_{0B}^4)$, at first order in $\epsilon_T$ and leading order in $\delta p_T$, $\kappa_A$, $\kappa_B$.

To second order in the plane-wave labels the tick ratio is the same function of the drift speed for both types iff $v^A_{\max}=v^B_{\max}$, that is iff $\tau_A\kappa_A\sigma_{X_A}=\tau_B\kappa_B\sigma_{X_B}$.

With the label eliminated, (5.29) reads $R_T^2(1-\beta_T^2)=1+(R_T^2-1)^2/\rho_T^2$, hence $R_T=1+\frac{\beta_T^2}{2}+\bigl(\frac38+\frac{1}{2\rho_T^2}\bigr)\beta_T^4+O(\beta_T^6)$ with $\beta_T=\nu/v^T_{\max}$, $\rho_T=\tau_T/\bar\mu_T$.

Under $v^A_{\max}=v^B_{\max}$: $R_A-R_B=\frac{\beta^4}{2}\bigl(\bar\mu_A^2/\tau_A^2-\bar\mu_B^2/\tau_B^2\bigr)+O(\beta^6)$; the relations (5.29) of the two types agree iff in addition $\bar\mu_A/\tau_A=\bar\mu_B/\tau_B$, so they do not agree in general.
For each type and each clock level, $I^T_k=M^T_k/(v^T_{\max})^2$, that is $M^T_k=I^T_k\,(v^T_{\max})^2$ with $M^T_k=m_T+\frac{2\pi k}{N_T\lambda_{0T}}$.

The relation between background inertia and rest cost is the same for both types, $M^A_k/I^A_k=M^B_{k'}/I^B_{k'}$ for all levels, iff $v^A_{\max}=v^B_{\max}$, that is iff $\tau_A\kappa_A\sigma_{X_A}=\tau_B\kappa_B\sigma_{X_B}$.
The condition (8.13) for a common leading-order tick-ratio law and the condition (8.17) for a common inertia-rest-cost relation are both equivalent to $v^A_{\max}=v^B_{\max}$.

open_issues: Equality of the maximal speeds is a condition on the description (8.9); nothing in this package selects it (out of scope).

Item 3 inherits the orders of 05-moving-clock and 06-inertia-internal-energy; beyond leading order in κ (out of scope) the influence of b on the view of a is of order κ_A κ_B, and the mean ⟨X_T⟩ can be rebooked by (8.1) as a uniform cost gradient on body T of first order in κ_T.
The maximal speed of a type is an upper bound; the drift speeds (5.25) of Model D do not exceed v_top < v_max, which depends on ρ_T as well, so equal v_max does not give equal v_top (8.15).
Only chain types and Model D types are compared, as the question asks; other types are covered only by (8.5), (8.6) and (8.9).

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions of v_max, β, ρ, R and I_k, and invariance of all results under the rescaling κ_T → sκ_T, X_T → X_T/s that leaves the records unchanged
Equal parameters of the two types (all conditions hold, (8.12) and (8.15) vanish) and exchange of a and b (Z → −Z, differences change sign, conditions symmetric)
Special case ρ_T = 1, sin²p₀ = 0.01: the expansion (8.14) gives R = 1.0049851 against the exact 1.0049876, a difference of order β⁶
